key_insight: WAAM repurposes conventional arc-welding physics—especially heat input, melt-pool dynamics, and solidification control—to build near-net-shape metal parts layer by layer.
engineering_relevance: The review helps engineers choose and tune GMAW, GTAW, or PAW variants to balance deposition rate, microstructure, defect risk, and surface quality in scalable metal additive manufacturing.
method: Physics-based review of WAAM as an adaptation of welding processes
Compares thermal/solidification behavior through G/R, heat distribution, and deposition strategy
Synthesizes arc transfer modes, defect mechanisms, and alloy-specific process choices
evidence_signal: The paper is a literature review that compiles governing equations and cross-system findings rather than reporting a new experimental dataset.
watch_item: Process selection is highly alloy- and geometry-dependent, so results from one WAAM setup may not transfer directly without recalibrating heat input and toolpath strategy.
paper_title: Application and Adaptation of Arc-Based Welding Processes to Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing: A Review
